keyVerseText: These are the sons of Dan after their families: of Shuham, the family of the Shuhamites. These are the families of Dan after their families.
rootMeaning: The root of שׁוּחָמִי (Shûwchâmîy) lies in the name שׁוּחָם (Shûwchâm), which means "pit-digger." This patronymic origin highlights a practical, labor-related identity tied to the ancestor Shuham, son of Dan. The literal sense of "pit-digger" suggests a grounded, industrious heritage that goes beyond the simple tribal name, connecting the family to tangible work and ancestral legacy.
usageInScripture: The term שׁוּחָמִי is used specifically to denote the descendants of Shuham, the son of Dan, appearing twice in Scripture. It consistently translates as "of the Shuhamites," indicating a collective family or clan identity. This focused usage underscores the importance of genealogical records in Israel, preserving tribal distinctions and heritage without variation in meaning.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding שׁוּחָמִי as the designation for the Shuhamite family enriches our grasp of God's providence in preserving Israel's tribal structure. Each name and lineage reflects God's sovereign orchestration of His people, emphasizing faithfulness to covenant promises through generational continuity. The root meaning, "pit-digger," reminds believers that God values the faithful labor and legacy of His people, who are called to build and cultivate His kingdom. This lineage points forward to the unity and diversity within God's redeemed community, ultimately fulfilled in Christ who gathers all tribes into one.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 26:42 states, "These are the sons of Dan after their families: of Shuham, the family of the Shuhamites." Here, שׁוּחָמִי identifies a specific clan within the tribe of Dan, emphasizing the ordered and intentional nature of God's people. The word anchors the verse in historical reality and familial identity, underscoring how God meticulously accounts for each family within His covenant community.
